newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Bitor sees 4.4 mln tonnes Orimulsion sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bitor sees 4.4 mln tonnes Orimulsion sales in 1997.

text.p: Venezuela's Bitumenes de Orinoco (Bitor), a unit of state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), sees sales of its trademark boiler fuel Orimulsion rising to 4.4 million tonnes in 1997, from about four million tonnes this year, a top company official said.

"We have estimated that sales will be 4.4 million tonnes for 1997 compared to four million this year," Eladio Bueno, head of marketing and sales, told reporters during a tour of the company's operations in central-eastern Venezuela.

Bitor has supply contracts for the bitumen-water mix fuel in the Great Britain (1.5 million tonnes), Japan (0.75 million), Denmark (one million), Canada (0.8 million) and Lithuania (0.5 million), Bueno said.

Bitor expects to sign further supply contracts with power generators in the United States, Great Britain, China and others to bring production to 20 million tonnes in 2000 and 32 million tonnes in 2005.
"Our market potential is about 60 million tonnes per year of which we are aiming to penetrate about half," Bueno said.
Vast bitumen reserves in Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt mean that Bitor could produce up to 100 tonnes per year for four centuries. "For practical purposes the reserves are inexhaustible," Bueno added.

Work should begin shortly on a second processing unit at Morichal. The $320 million plant is to be built and operated by a joint venture between Bitor (40 percent), DuPont unit Conoco (30 percent), Norway's Statoil (20 percent) and Venezuela's Jandis.

The plant would have a capacity of five million tonnes per year, most of which was intended for Florida Power and Light's Manatee plant in Florida. Florida's High State Commission rejected use of the boiler fuel in April, a ruling which Florida Power is appealing.
